title: "Poisson Distribution: Sum of Distributions"

## Visualizing the Sum of Independent Poisson Distributions

The provided R script demonstrates a key property of Poisson distributions: the sum of two independent Poisson random variables is also a Poisson random variable.

The code does this by first defining two independent Poisson distributions with rate parameters, or λ values, of $\lambda_1 = 3$ and $\lambda_2 = 5$. It then calculates and plots the Probability Mass Function (PMF) and the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) for each of these individual distributions, as well as for their sum.

The resulting plots visually confirm that the summed distribution is a Poisson distribution with a new rate parameter of $\lambda = 8$, which is the sum of the individual rates (3 + 5). The plots also include vertical lines to highlight the average of each distribution, further illustrating the relationship.

```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# This script demonstrates that the sum of two independent Poisson random variables
# is also a Poisson random variable, with a rate parameter equal to the sum
# of the individual rate parameters.

# Load the necessary library for plotting
# The 'tidyverse' package is a good choice for this as it includes ggplot2.
# If you don't have it installed, run: install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)

# --- 1. Define the Parameters ---

# Let's set the rate parameters for our two independent Poisson distributions.
# We'll use lambda_1 = 3 and lambda_2 = 5 for this example.
lambda1 <- 3
lambda2 <- 5

# The rate parameter for the sum of the two distributions will be the sum
# of the individual rate parameters.
lambda_sum <- lambda1 + lambda2

# Define the range of k (number of events) to plot.
# We choose a range that extends well beyond the expected values to show
# the full shape of the distributions.
k_values <- 0:20


# --- 2. Calculate the PMFs ---

# The PMF of a Poisson distribution is given by:
# P(X=k) = (e^(-lambda) * lambda^k) / k!

# Calculate the PMF for the first Poisson distribution, X1.
pmf1 <- dpois(k_values, lambda = lambda1)

# Calculate the PMF for the second Poisson distribution, X2.
pmf2 <- dpois(k_values, lambda = lambda2)

# Calculate the PMF for the sum, X_sum = X1 + X2.
# This should follow a Poisson distribution with the sum of the rates.
pmf_sum <- dpois(k_values, lambda = lambda_sum)


# --- 3. Create a Data Frame for Plotting ---

# We'll combine all the PMF data into a single data frame for easy plotting
# with ggplot2.
df_pmf <- tibble(
  k = k_values,
  pmf1 = pmf1,
  pmf2 = pmf2,
  pmf_sum = pmf_sum
)


# --- 4. Plot the PMFs ---

# Reshape the data for plotting with ggplot2, which works best with a
# "long" data format.
df_pmf_long <- df_pmf %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pmf1, pmf2, pmf_sum),
    names_to = "distribution",
    values_to = "probability"
  )

# Define a color palette for the plots.
color_palette <- c("pmf1" = "#1f78b4", "pmf2" = "#a6cee3", "pmf_sum" = "#33a02c")
legend_labels <- c(
  "pmf1" = "Poisson(λ=3)",
  "pmf2" = "Poisson(λ=5)",
  "pmf_sum" = "Sum: Poisson(λ=8)"
)

# Plot the PMFs
pmf_plot <- ggplot(df_pmf_long, aes(x = k, y = probability, fill = distribution)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "PMFs of Two Poisson Distributions and Their Sum",
    x = "Number of Events (k)",
    y = "Probability P(X=k)",
    fill = "Distribution"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(k_values), max(k_values), by = 1)) +
  # Add vertical lines for mean and median
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda1, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf1"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(df_pmf$pmf1), linetype = "dotted", color = color_palette["pmf1"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda2, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf2"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(df_pmf$pmf2), linetype = "dotted", color = color_palette["pmf2"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda_sum, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf_sum"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(df_pmf$pmf_sum), linetype = "dotted", color = color_palette["pmf_sum"], linewidth = 1)


# --- 5. Calculate the CDFs ---

# The CDF of a Poisson distribution is the cumulative probability,
# i.e., P(X <= k) = sum(P(X=i)) for i=0 to k.
# R's ppois() function calculates this for us.

# Calculate the CDF for the first Poisson distribution, X1.
cdf1 <- ppois(k_values, lambda = lambda1)

# Calculate the CDF for the second Poisson distribution, X2.
cdf2 <- ppois(k_values, lambda = lambda2)

# Calculate the CDF for the sum, X_sum = X1 + X2.
# This should also follow a Poisson distribution.
cdf_sum <- ppois(k_values, lambda = lambda_sum)


# --- 6. Create a Data Frame for Plotting the CDFs ---

df_cdf <- tibble(
  k = k_values,
  cdf1 = cdf1,
  cdf2 = cdf2,
  cdf_sum = cdf_sum
)

# Reshape the data for plotting with ggplot2
df_cdf_long <- df_cdf %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cdf1, cdf2, cdf_sum),
    names_to = "distribution",
    values_to = "probability"
  )


# --- 7. Plot the CDFs ---

cdf_plot <- ggplot(df_cdf_long, aes(x = k, y = probability, color = distribution, fill = distribution)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "CDFs of Two Poisson Distributions and Their Sum",
    x = "Number of Events (k)",
    y = "Cumulative Probability P(X≤k)",
    color = "Distribution"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette, labels = legend_labels) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(k_values), max(k_values), by = 1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  # Add vertical lines for mean and median
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda1, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf1"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda2, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf2"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = lambda_sum, linetype = "dashed", color = color_palette["pmf_sum"], linewidth = 1) 

# --- 8. Display the plots ---

# Print the plots to the R console or graphics device
print(pmf_plot)
print(cdf_plot)
```
